# Custer County Courthouse (South Dakota)

The Custer County Courthouse is a historic governmental building located in **Custer, South Dakota**, the county seat of Custer County.

## Historical Significance

- The courthouse was listed on the **National Register of Historic Places** in 1975.
- It is one of the notable historic structures in the Black Hills region of South Dakota.

## Architecture and Construction

- The courthouse was built in **1881**, making it one of the older courthouses in South Dakota.
- It is a **stone construction** building, built from locally quarried stone, reflecting the building materials and construction methods common in the Black Hills during the late 19th century.
- The architecture reflects a **vernacular/frontier style** typical of government buildings constructed in the Dakota Territory era.

## Context

- Custer County was established in 1875, and the town of Custer is one of the oldest settlements in the Black Hills, having been founded during the **Black Hills Gold Rush** following the 1874 Custer Expedition led by George Armstrong Custer.
- The courthouse served the governmental and judicial needs of the county during a period of rapid growth associated with mining and settlement in the region.

## Current Status

The building has been preserved as a historic landmark and is recognized for its role in the early governmental history of western South Dakota.

If you're looking for more specific architectural details or recent developments regarding the building, local historical societies or the South Dakota State Historic Preservation Office would be excellent resources.
